asr.full_text: Welcome back to Good Day Atlanta Gift cards are a top pick for holiday or birthday gifts but some people who unwrap them over Christmas are just now finding out that the Grinch has stole the money The Fox 5's I-team's Dana Fallows here with how crooks have created another way to steal your money Good morning to you and what have they come up with now I know, this is their job You know that barcode that you're going to find on the back of your gift card Well, it could be fake! Placed there by Crooks The National Consumers League says it's a problem hitting retailers and consumers nationwide. We talked to a metro area family who bought $1,500 in gift cards for loved ones, but the money went to strangers. We went into a grocery store, and purchased three gift cards for family members for Christmas. Pretty ordinary. Debbie Daniels' husband put $500 a piece on three gift cards for a total of $1500. They wrap them up, and send them off. Nothing unusual. It was a Visa gift card plucked from a grocery store carousel. LYNN LITTLEBEE, ST. My sister-in-law Lynn went in, opened the gift card, and saw that it was not a Visa gift card, but it was, in fact, a Walmart gift card. Now, it was in the packaging, right? Like, she had to tear it open. LYNN LITTLEBEE, ST. She had to open it up. It was in a visa gift card jacket jacket the other two gift recipients found the same thing...what appeared to be a Walmart gift card inside a sealed Visa package obviously thats odd but they went ahead and tried to use it anyway at Walmart i mean 500 bucks is 500 bucks right wrong... and the person said, I'm sorry, this card is has not been activated. But how can this happen? It was a gift card, presumably sealed in the original jacket. But inside of this Visa packaging again is an empty Walmart card. According to the Better Business Bureau, this was a hot holiday scam and this strip of paper, is the key to how it works. It's a barcode. It's taped over the dud Walmart barcode and it belongs to the Visa gift card the Daniels thought was in there. So you did put five hundred dollars on this? Yes, we put five hundred dollars that activate on that barcode. Who has this card? We don't know. The Fox 5 Eye Team reached out to Wal-Mart and Visa about this happening, and Visa wrote, talk to the merchant. So we did and got great consumer advice. The cards were purchased at a Suburban Kroger. But the scam impacts many, many retailers. The Kroger spokesman said in an email, thanks for making consumers aware of this problem. They blame organized retail crime rings for this gift card scam, and here's how you can protect yourself. Kroger recommends rubbing a nail across that barcode to make sure it's raised. You should feel it. If it's a copy, it'll be smooth. Also make sure your gift recipient has that activation receipt for reference. Meantime, Debbie posted to social media, Buyer Beware, letting her circle of friends know there's a new scam in town. Don't be a victim. I'll look at it a little bit more carefully because we do buy gift cards on a regular basis for different people. Let me just say, she's going to continue to go to her Kroger. She's going to continue to buy gift cards. The Daniels paid for those large purchases, though, totaling $1,500 with the credit card, which means they could get their money back. Their credit card company is investigating. I hope so. And you showed us there about those barcodes and how they can be faked. Can you kind of show us? Yeah, a real difference you rub your thumb over it can you feel it yeah it feels raised edges this in the packaging that's the fake one smooth smooth very smooth so you get if you just rub your finger over it you can tell the difference I went in to right away or picked one up I'm found up what looked like a janky one myself, turned it into the retailer, and it seemed obvious. Doesn't hurt to try at least. Just do it. One more layer of protection that you are in control of. Great information Dana, thank you very much.
